stem_book: Consider a cylinder of mass M and radius R lying on a rough horizontal plane. It has a plank lying on its top as shown in figure. A force F is applied on the plank such that the plank moves and causes the cylinder to roll. The plank always remains horizontal. There is no slipping at any point of contact. Calculate the acceleration of the cylinder and the frictional forces at the two contacts.
key: a = 4F cosθ/(3M+8m); f plank = 3MF cosθ/(3M+8m); f ground = MF cosθ/(3M+8m)
derived: a = 4F cosθ/(3M + 8m); f₁ = 3MF cosθ/(3M + 8m); f₂ = MF cosθ/(3M + 8m)
correct_answer: a = 4F cosθ/(3M + 8m); f_plank = 3MF cosθ/(3M + 8m); f_ground = MF cosθ/(3M + 8m)
reason: 'as shown in figure' but no figure is printed - the plank mass m and the angle θ of F (used by the key) are never given; also three separate answers
work: plank a_p = 2a: F cosθ − f₁ = 2ma; cylinder f₁ + f₂ = Ma, (f₁ − f₂)R = (MR²/2)(a/R) ⇒ f₁ = 3Ma/4, f₂ = Ma/4 ⇒ a = 4F cosθ/(3M + 8m)
